messages.subject: Re: חיסור בין שני עמודות בין dataframe-ים שונים
parts:
Hi Lior,
Not sure I understand.
If you have a dataframe df1 with 100 rows and dataframe df2 with 130 rows, what should be the result of subtracting one column from the other?
Basically R supports vector operations so there's no need to write loops. For example, assuming that both data frames have the same number of rows:

z <- df1$x > df2$x

would give you a vector of TRUE and FALSE for each row.

If you subtract to vectors of unequal lengths, you'd get the result only for some rows and a warning message:
> df1 <- data.frame(x = rnorm(100))
> df2 <- data.frame(x = rnorm(130))
> z <- (df1$x - df2$x) > 1

Warning message:
In df1$x > df2$x :
  longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length

If one data frame has a length that is a multiple of the second (e.g. 100 and 200), R would reuse the smaller vector again:

df1 <- data.frame(x = rnorm(100))
df2 <- data.frame(x = rnorm(200))
z <- (df1$x - df2$x) > 1
(no warning message even though df1 and df2 have different lengths).

Hope this helps.
Omri
